newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica KWV privatisation delayed after court deal.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica KWV privatisation delayed after court deal.

text.p: South Africa's Cape Supreme Court on Thursday postponed to March 25 rival applications from wine co-operative KWV and Agriculture Minister Derek Hanekom on the future of the organisation.
A ministry spokesman said that the two parties had agreed to the postponement before the ruling was made.
KWV had been applying for permission to change its status from a statutory co-operative to a private company by the end of April.
Hanekom had applied for this permission to be postponed until he could consult more widely to ensure it was in the best interests of the wine sector.
Hanekom said he had decided to obtain the order because he wanted to "ensure that a proper regulatory framework is in place with regard to the wine and distilling industry."
Hanekom said KWV's current plans threatened the integrity of the existing system.

"I am concerned that moneys and resources which were accumulated for the purposes of the KWV's regulatory function might be distributed amongst present KWV members as part of their scheme of arrangement," he added.
Hanekom said he hoped the matter could be settled through talks and there would be no need for litigation.

"In the event of the matter being settled by agreement or in the event of the courts making an appropriate ruling, I will as soon as possible begin a broad consultative process within the industry," he said.

The KWV, which is believed to have assets of about two billion rand, last week announced that 4,751 of its members had approved a plan to convert the co-operative into a company from But several wine industry analysts have expressed concern about the plan as the KWV has been a statutory body and had built up its assets on the basis of the control it had over the industry.
